prompt:
Add a complete, opt-in CSS class namespace to Python-Markdown so multiple independently styled documents can coexist on a page. This is a library-wide rendering feature.

Public API: Markdown(..., class_prefix='') and markdown.markdown(..., class_prefix='') accept the option. Markdown.class_prefix exposes it. The empty string is the default and preserves existing HTML exactly. A nonempty prefix must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*; reject invalid strings with ValueError and non-string values with TypeError. Keep the prefix for the life of the converter, including reset() and repeated conversions. Different converters must remain independent.

Apply the prefix to each CSS class token generated by the bundled extensions: footnotes (container, reference and backlinks including repeated references), admonition (container, type tokens, title and nested blocks), fenced_code (language classes and configurable language prefix), codehilite (configured wrapper class tokens on the Pygments and fallback paths, including fenced-code integration), toc (container, optional title, heading anchor and permalink classes including configurable values and multiple tokens), and wikilinks (configured HTML class). A configured built-in class such as toc_class='outline compact' becomes two prefixed tokens. Existing extension options continue to work, and empty optional class strings stay empty. Include the extra extension bundle and compositions with attr_list, md_in_html, meta and sane_lists. A small shared mechanism is welcome if it avoids inconsistent treatment, but class ownership must remain explicit.

Only classes created as structural or language decoration by these bundled extensions are in scope. Preserve classes written explicitly in Markdown attribute lists or raw HTML, including names that happen to match a built-in class; preserve class-looking text, code contents, IDs, hrefs, heading slugs, footnote identifiers and all Unicode user content. Additional explicit classes on a fenced block stay unchanged while its generated language class gets the prefix. Pygments owns its internal token and highlighted-line classes: preserve those and only namespace the wrapper owned by Python-Markdown. Third-party extensions' arbitrary class attributes stay unchanged. Do not rewrite final HTML with a regex, blanket-prefix every class in the tree, mutate global extension defaults, or rely on process-global state.

Audit intermediate representations as well as final output. In particular Markdown.toc and the inserted [TOC] tree must agree, optional heading links must retain their IDs and destinations, nested admonitions must still be parsed, and codehilite must keep highlighting and escaping intact. The same source should render correctly with empty and nonempty prefixes in alternating converter instances and after reset.

Add focused tests in the relevant existing test modules plus integration tests covering mixed extensions, custom multi-token classes, converter reuse, collisions with explicit user classes, fenced and indented code, Pygments on and off, HTML/xHTML serializers, Unicode and nested structures. Update core API documentation and the affected extension documentation with precedence, ownership boundaries and a runnable example combining several extensions. Run the full project test suite and the available relevant style checks, fixing regressions introduced by this feature. Preserve the project's supported Python versions and coding conventions. Complete the feature across the listed extensions and finish with a concise report of implementation and verification. Make ordinary implementation choices autonomously.
